provenance.title: WHO mhGAP priority mental-health conditions — assess, and escalate the one that cannot wait
provenance.why: The mhGAP Intervention Guide lets a non-specialist recognise and manage the priority mental, neurological and substance-use conditions where most of the burden and most of the treatment gap sit. The rule that cannot be softened is the one at the top: imminent risk of self-harm or suicide is a same-day emergency, and the correct response is to keep the person safe and not leave them alone — every other priority condition is assessed and managed, but a person with a suicidal plan or a high self-harm risk must never be allowed to leave the encounter as an ordinary, overridable notification. The remaining rules — moderate-to-severe depression, psychosis, harmful substance use, and epilepsy/seizure — open a management or referral pathway rather than an emergency one. Mental-health content of this kind is sensitive by nature (SPECIALLY_PROTECTED); the note below records that so downstream surfaces treat it accordingly, but this pack carries no access-control logic — confidentiality is enforced by the trust plane, not by clinical content.

sourceVerification.note: The WHO mhGAP Intervention Guide v2.0 (2016) is NOT vendored under docs/reference/who-dak/MANIFEST.json. This pack was authored against the published master chart and the DEP/PSY/SUB/EPI/SUI modules rather than extracted from a pinned artefact, so it ships ENGINEERING_SEED and blocks ratification until the primary text is vendored and the thresholds are ratified by MOHCC. The caller facts here (selfHarmRisk, suicidalPlan, depressionModerateSevere, psychosisFeatures, substanceUseHarmful, seizureConvulsion, mhAssessmentConducted) are structured-assessment outputs, not raw clinical text; their coded vocabularies are placeholders pending the national mental-health assessment forms. This content is SPECIALLY_PROTECTED by nature — the sensitivity is noted for downstream handling only and no access-control decision is made here.

rules.name: Imminent self-harm / suicide risk — same-day safety response, do not leave alone
rules.message: Imminent risk of self-harm or suicide — respond today and do not leave this person alone.
rules.explanation: In mhGAP, a high assessed risk of self-harm or a current suicidal plan is a medical emergency, not a routine finding. The immediate priorities are to keep the person physically safe, remove access to means, mobilise a support person, and arrange urgent specialist review — before any other priority condition is worked up. Because acting on this cannot be deferred, this alert is interruptive and cannot be overridden away as an ordinary notification.
rules.requiredAction: Do not leave the person alone. Remove access to means of self-harm, offer and activate psychosocial support, and arrange urgent same-day mental-health specialist assessment. Document the safety plan and the person contacted to stay with them.
sourceRefs: WHO mhGAP Intervention Guide v2.0 (2016) — Self-harm / suicide (SUI) module; assessment and management of imminent risk

adaptation.whoStatement: A person at imminent risk of self-harm or suicide must not be left alone; remove access to means and arrange urgent specialist care.
adaptation.nationalStatement: Adopted as an interruptive, non-overridable same-day safety response pending national mental-health emergency pathway definition.
adaptation.rationale: Non-verbatim: the WHO management step is expressed here as a non-overridable interruptive alert so the do-not-leave-alone action cannot be dismissed as a routine notification. The clinical instruction is unchanged; only its enforcement posture is made explicit.
evidenceRefs: WHO mhGAP Intervention Guide v2.0 (2016) — SUI module

testCases.name: high assessed self-harm risk fires the emergency response
a current suicidal plan fires even when overall risk was scored lower
neither risk fact assessed — a red flag must never fire on absent data
risk assessed and low with no plan does not fire

rules.name: Moderate-to-severe depression — start structured treatment
rules.message: Moderate-to-severe depression — begin a structured treatment plan.
rules.explanation: Where a mental-health assessment identifies moderate-to-severe depression, mhGAP directs the non-specialist to start management: psychoeducation, a brief psychological intervention where available, consideration of an antidepressant, and follow-up. Mild presentations are watched and supported rather than medicated; this rule fires only for the moderate-to-severe band.
rules.requiredAction: Provide psychoeducation and a brief structured psychological intervention where available, consider antidepressant therapy per the national formulary, address concurrent self-harm risk, and schedule follow-up to review response.
sourceRefs: WHO mhGAP Intervention Guide v2.0 (2016) — Depression (DEP) module; assessment and management protocol

adaptation.whoStatement: Offer treatment for moderate-to-severe depression; mild depression should not be treated with antidepressants routinely.
evidenceRefs: WHO mhGAP Intervention Guide v2.0 (2016) — DEP module

testCases.name: assessment done and moderate-to-severe depression identified fires
assessment done but depression band not recorded — must not fire on absent data
assessment done and not moderate-to-severe does not fire
no mental-health assessment conducted — rule does not apply

rules.name: Features of psychosis — assess and start treatment or refer
rules.message: Features of psychosis present — assess, start antipsychotic treatment or refer.
rules.explanation: When an assessment finds features of psychosis — delusions, hallucinations, disorganised thinking or grossly abnormal behaviour — mhGAP directs the non-specialist to exclude a medical or substance-induced cause, start an antipsychotic where competent to do so, and arrange specialist review. Early treatment improves outcome, so this opens a management-plus-referral pathway.
rules.requiredAction: Exclude an acute medical or substance-induced cause, start antipsychotic treatment per the national formulary where competent, engage the family/carer, and refer for specialist mental-health assessment.
sourceRefs: WHO mhGAP Intervention Guide v2.0 (2016) — Psychoses (PSY) module; assessment and management protocol

adaptation.whoStatement: Assess for psychosis; start antipsychotic medication and refer for specialist review where features are present.
evidenceRefs: WHO mhGAP Intervention Guide v2.0 (2016) — PSY module

testCases.name: assessment done and psychosis features present fires
assessment done but psychosis features not recorded — must not fire on absent data
assessment done and no psychosis features does not fire
no mental-health assessment conducted — rule does not apply

rules.name: Harmful alcohol or drug use screen positive — brief intervention
rules.message: Harmful alcohol or drug use identified — deliver a brief intervention.
rules.explanation: A positive screen for harmful use of alcohol or other substances is the point at which mhGAP recommends a structured brief intervention — feedback, motivational discussion and a plan to reduce use — with referral reserved for dependence or complicated withdrawal. Catching harmful use before dependence is where a short conversation changes the trajectory.
rules.requiredAction: Deliver a structured brief intervention (feedback, advice, goal-setting), assess for dependence and withdrawal risk, and refer to specialist substance-use services if dependence or complicated withdrawal is present.
sourceRefs: WHO mhGAP Intervention Guide v2.0 (2016) — Disorders due to substance use (SUB) module; brief intervention

adaptation.whoStatement: Offer a brief intervention to people with harmful use of alcohol or drugs; refer those with dependence.
evidenceRefs: WHO mhGAP Intervention Guide v2.0 (2016) — SUB module

testCases.name: assessment done and harmful use screen positive fires
assessment done but substance-use screen not recorded — must not fire on absent data
assessment done and screen negative does not fire
no mental-health assessment conducted — rule does not apply

rules.name: Convulsive seizure / epilepsy — assess and manage or refer
rules.message: Convulsive seizure reported — assess for epilepsy and manage or refer.
rules.explanation: Epilepsy is an mhGAP priority condition because it is common, treatable, and heavily stigmatised. A reported convulsive seizure prompts a check for an acute cause, first-aid and safety counselling, consideration of antiepileptic treatment once a diagnosis of epilepsy is established, and referral where the diagnosis or the seizure type is uncertain.
rules.requiredAction: Exclude an acute provoked cause (fever, hypoglycaemia, head injury, eclampsia), give seizure first-aid and safety advice, consider antiepileptic treatment once epilepsy is established, and refer for confirmation where the diagnosis is uncertain.
sourceRefs: WHO mhGAP Intervention Guide v2.0 (2016) — Epilepsy (EPI) module; assessment and management protocol

adaptation.whoStatement: Assess a person with convulsive seizures for epilepsy; exclude acute causes, and treat or refer.
evidenceRefs: WHO mhGAP Intervention Guide v2.0 (2016) — EPI module

testCases.name: assessment done and a convulsive seizure reported fires
assessment done but seizure history not recorded — must not fire on absent data
assessment done and no seizure does not fire
no mental-health assessment conducted — rule does not apply
